title: Linear-Time Canonical Header Test
statement: For every machine format $F$, there exist a finite Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet and a constant $a\\in\\mathbb N$ such that, on every Boolean word $\\alpha$, $M$ halts after exactly $a(|\\alpha|+1)$ steps and outputs the one-bit word whose bit is true exactly when the last bit of the parsed header (defaulting to true if that header is empty) is true.
hypotheses_covered: output is the one-bit canonical-bits test of the parsed header
